text:
ajay: Heads-up — prod started returning generic 'payload too large' rejections from /v1/embeddings for requests that contain mixed vector lengths. Console shows a 413 with no routing or shape info. Repro logs below.

maria: Seen similar traces. Router seems to reject when either total bytes > shard_limit OR when input shapes are heterogeneous. The error surfaces too late.

kevin: Quick clarifying q: are clients sending a single request with items that have different vector lengths (e.g., 512 and 768)? Can you paste a minimal repro?

ajay: Yup. Example we got from a customer (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"inputs": [{"text":"short","vector_length":512},{"text":"longer","vector_length":768}]}'
```
Response: 413 Payload Too Large + body: {"error":"payload too large"} (no hint whether it was bytes vs shape).

nina: We should fail fast with a clearer status. Proposal: return 422 + error_code = "mixed_vector_lengths" when shapes conflict OR 413 if strictly a bytes limit. Include machine-readable fields: `error_hint`, `accepted_routes` (list of route ids/regions that would succeed), and `suggested_action` (split/single-model). Also surface a header: `X-Embed-Debug: route_attempts=3;fallback=none`.

sam: Agreed. Also for telemetry/metrics we need: `embed.request_count`, `embed.input_count`, `embed.total_bytes`, `embed.max_vector_length`, `embed.shard_rejects`, `embed.route_try_count`, `embed.fallback_reason`. That lets us graph whether it's bytes-driven or dim-driven.

maria: Console UX idea: when a request fails, show a small diagnostics pane: "Diagnostics: inputs=3, vector_lengths=[512,768,512], total_bytes=4.2MB, suggested_split=2 requests". Link to doc page about the splitter and SDK helpers. Also show per-route attempts and which route rejected.

kevin: Implementation idea: add a lightweight server preflight endpoint (or a header `X-Embed-Preflight: 1`) that returns a 200 + JSON with `route_hints` and `batching_strategy` without incurring full execution cost. That lets SDKs auto-split before hitting router. Feature-flag this behind `embed_preflight`.

ajay: Rollout plan suggestion: enable `embed_preflight` for 10% of traffic first (canary), watch `embed.shard_rejects` & latency, 50% week 2, GA on stable metrics. Backfill telemetry for at least 7 days so we can decide on console defaults.

deploy-bot: Created INF-3987 (embed preflight + clearer errors). Canary config: embed-router v2 -> ring=10% scheduled.

nina: I'll draft the API error schema and console wireframes. Error body example I'm thinking:
```json
{
  "error": "mixed_vector_lengths",
  "error_hint": "inputs have varying vector_length: [512,768]",
  "suggested_action": "split_by_vector_length",
  "accepted_routes": ["route-a-eu", "route-b-us-west"]
}
```

sam: Also include `suggested_retry: true/false` (true if there's an automatic fallback route) so SDKs can decide whether to retry split or fail fast.

kevin: Dev tasks: parse optional headers (X-Embed-Preflight, X-Client-Vector-Length), add preflight handler that returns routing hints, and produce OTLP spans with the new attributes. I'll put up a PR with tests.

ajay: Action list: nina -> error spec + console mock; kevin -> preflight + header parsing; sam -> telemetry metrics + OTLP attribute names; maria -> add console diagnostic panel copy; all -> review PRs. Thanks y'all.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll start the console mock this afternoon.

deploy-bot: Note: canary deployment scheduled for 2025-09-17 18:00 UTC.

ajay: Nice. One more: prefer returning 422 for semantic input errors and reserve 413 for raw-bytes-limit. Keeps client logic deterministic.

kevin: Agreed. I'll map server responses accordingly in the router.

sam: I'll add dashboards: count of 422 vs 413, top offending client versions, and a heatmap of vector_length distributions.

ajay: Perfect — closing thread, please add your PR links into INF-3987 when ready.
